long_biography.plain_text:
Dutch entrepreneur Gerard van Leest directed Aquaparx, a supplier of water leisure equipment ranging from inflatable boats to floating playgrounds. At its European distribution centre in Zevenaar, he showed visitors how the business combined a broad product range with its own materials production. Keeping production costs down was intended to make its boats accessible to more customers.

As a floating playground at Vlietland prepared to open, he explained the practical controls for children using its linked slides, climbing frames and trampolines. Lifejackets were compulsory, and an electronic counting system monitored visitor numbers against the site's capacity. Entry also depended on age, height and swimming ability.
